LESSON: PLANTS AND ITS RESOURCES

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Environment
Topic 1.4: Plants and its resources

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Plants and its resources. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PLANTS AND ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Plants and its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants

What this means
In this part you learn to Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Plants and its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Plants and its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Plants and its resources” around your school. (skill: Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Plants and its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Plants and its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Plants and its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Plants and its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Plants and its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Identify different types of plants edible, thorny/non-thorny, poisonous/non- plants.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
